02
About the Hotel

A Modern Stay
in Central Medan

Hotel Santika Premiere Dyandra Medan is a four-star hotel and convention property on Jl. Kapten Maulana Lubis No. 7, in the heart of Medan City Center within easy reach of landmarks such as Grand City Hall, Sun Plaza and the historic Tjong A Fie Mansion. Public tourism and travel-booking information lists accommodation, dining, an outdoor pool, a business center, a convention center and other guest services on site.

But a hotel is more than its facilities. Here, comfort is intended to be the starting point of the stay, not the whole story a base from which guests can taste, learn and connect with the culture of North Sumatra before they even leave the building.

Accommodation

Rooms Designed
for Comfort

Public hotel-booking platforms describe Hotel Santika Premiere Dyandra Medan as a property of over 300 guest rooms, arranged across several categories from Superior and Deluxe rooms to Premier rooms and Suites. Listed in-room comforts commonly include air conditioning, a work desk, an in-room safe, a flat-screen television, premium bedding and complimentary bottled water, with higher categories reported to include extras such as a deep soaking bathtub.

04
Hotel Facilities & Services

Everything a Modern
Stay Needs

Alongside its guest rooms, public travel-booking listings describe the hotel as offering a restaurant and bar/lounge, a coffee shop, an outdoor swimming pool, a 24-hour business center, valet and self-parking, daily housekeeping, and a convention center with several meeting rooms reported to include a function hall capable of hosting large-scale events.

Convention & Meetings

Multiple meeting rooms and a function hall support conferences, weddings and community gatherings part of what the hotel's booking listings describe as its convention facilities.

Pool & Leisure

An outdoor pool offers a place to unwind between meetings or sightseeing, alongside on-site dining options for breakfast, lunch and dinner.

Business & Concierge

A 24-hour business center, front desk and concierge service are listed to assist guests travelling for work as well as leisure.

05
Food & Beverage

Ulos Café &
the Taste of Batak Heritage

A hospitality case study describes Ulos Café as a semi-open restaurant within the hotel, carrying a modern Batak-inspired touch in its design and service. Current listings also identify Kafe Ulos as a café located inside Hotel Santika Premiere Dyandra Medan.

The name is not incidental. Ulos is the traditional hand-woven cloth of the Batak people of North Sumatra literally translated as "blanket" and it is given at births, weddings and other milestones as a symbol of blessing, protection and belonging within Batak adat, or customary law. Naming a café after it carries a simple idea into the dining room: hospitality here is meant to wrap around a guest the way an ulos wraps around its wearer.

Semi-Open DiningBatak-InspiredCultural Heritage

Arsik

Arsik is a well-known Batak dish built on fish and a distinctive spice profile, commonly described as seasoned with andaliman a citrus-peppery pepper native to the Batak highlands. As a traditional dish, it can be made available specially for certain occasions at the hotel, such as:

Featured Menu for Special EventsA la Carte Menu / Seasonal PromoSpecial Order System (By Request)

One cup of coffee, one thread of heritage.

06
Eco-Hospitality

Comfort That
Respects the Land

North Sumatra's identity is inseparable from places like Lake Toba, one of the largest volcanic lakes in the world, and the highlands and rice terraces that surround it. Every guest who visits Medan is, in a small way, a guest of this wider landscape too.

Like many hotels operating across Indonesia, everyday sustainability in hospitality is commonly built from simple, practical habits: reusing towels and linens on request, conserving water and energy in guest rooms, managing waste responsibly, and sourcing ingredients including regional dishes such as arsik from local producers where possible. These practices reflect common eco-hospitality standards in the industry rather than a confirmed, hotel-specific program.

We invite you to travel a little lighter reuse a towel, mind the tap, and carry a habit of conservation with you beyond checkout.

SustainabilityConservationCommunity-Based SourcingEco-Conscious Hospitality
07
Local Cultural Identity

Local Culture
in Hospitality

"Modern comfort can become a doorway to local culture."

Malay Connection

ANTARA reported that in 2023, the hotel collaborated with Istana Maimun the historic Maimun Palace of the Deli Sultanate in the "Melayu Berkharisma" cultural program, which included exhibitions of Malay traditional clothing, historical objects, local UMKM (small business) products, and related cultural and art activities.

Indigenous Heritage

From the ulos cloth referenced in the café's name to the andaliman spice in arsik, indigenous Batak and Malay traditions are woven deliberately into the everyday guest experience, not set aside as a separate attraction.

A hotel can also become a space for cultural encounter: a place where a business traveller or a family on holiday can, in passing, learn what an ulos means, taste a regional spice, or stand where a sultanate once received its guests.

08
Guest Handling

A Warm
Local Hospitality

Guest handling at Hotel Santika Premiere Dyandra Medan focuses on clear communication, friendly assistance and attention to each guest's needs throughout the stay.

Warm WelcomeGuest AssistanceClear InformationPersonalized Service

Guest Journey

1. Arrival & Welcome → greet the guest warmly, confirm the reservation and assist with check-in.

2. Room Assistance → provide clear information about the room, hotel facilities and available services.

3. During the Stay → respond to guest requests, provide directions and assist with dining, facilities or other hotel services.

4. Guest Support → listen to concerns, provide suitable assistance and follow up when needed.

5. Check-out → confirm the bill, assist with departure and close the stay with a warm farewell.
